label: Addis Ababa
sub: Federal capital — seat of the Prosperity Party government; site of NEBE's June 22 declaration of a landslide parliamentary win

label: Mekelle
sub: Tigray regional capital — hit by dual drone strikes on Aug 20, 2026 that wounded 13 in the Hawelti Sub-City; also site of the May 5 reconstitution of the Tigray State Council and Debretsion Gebremichael's swearing-in as regional president

label: Mekelle University Area
sub: Second drone strike site reported by TPLF the same morning as the Hawelti Sub-City strike, Aug 20, 2026

label: Shererina
sub: Site of the August 1, 2026 ENDF-TPLF battle involving drones, artillery, and mechanized units — the most serious clash since the 2022 Pretoria agreement

label: Humera
sub: Western Tigray border town near Shererina; refugee flows toward Sudan intensified after the August 1 fighting

label: Tselemt (Tselemti)
sub: Disputed Tigray-Amhara boundary woreda; TDF crossed the Tekeze River here on Jan 26-29, 2026, triggering the year's first clashes

label: Alamata
sub: Southern Tigray town captured by Tigrayan forces on Jan 30, 2026 after federal command post withdrawal

label: Korem
sub: Southern Tigray town taken alongside Alamata on Jan 30, 2026

label: Merewa (Raya Alamata)
sub: Merewa Secondary School hit by drone strike Aug 10, 2026; Tigrayan military and the local governor gave conflicting casualty accounts

label: Enticho
sub: Drone strike hit two trucks near Enticho on Jan 31, 2026, killing one and injuring another

label: Gendebta
sub: Second site struck alongside Enticho on Jan 31, 2026

label: Raya Azebo
sub: Southern Tigray woreda; scene of TPLF allegations of federal drone strikes preceding the 2026 escalation

label: Axum
sub: Site of the TPLF Central Committee's mid-April emergency session that preceded the party's rejection of the interim administration

label: Wukro
sub: Tigray district that publicly endorsed the TPLF's April 2026 rejection of the interim administration

label: Shiraro
sub: Northwestern Tigray district that endorsed the TPLF's position rejecting the federally-extended interim administration

label: Bahir Dar
sub: Amhara regional capital; Fano offensives since March 2026 contested the B22 and B31 approach roads to the city

label: Debre Tabor (South Gondar)
sub: South Gondar zone capital; target of the ENDF's ~20,000-troop counteroffensive launched March 30, 2026

label: Debre Berhan (North Shewa)
sub: North Shewa zone; ENDF drone strike killed a pregnant woman, her 6-year-old daughter, and a young man in early February 2026

label: Debre Markos (East Gojjam)
sub: East Gojjam zone; drone strike on Feb 20, 2026 killed 16 people including children and injured 10

label: Assab, Eritrea
sub: Red Sea port Ethiopia has repeatedly signaled intent to regain access to; subject of reported Egyptian port-upgrade investment and Egypt-Eritrea maritime pact in 2026

label: Asmara, Eritrea
sub: Eritrean capital; President Isaias Afwerki accused Ethiopia of preparing for war over Red Sea access in a July 19, 2026 interview

label: Massawa, Eritrea
sub: Second Eritrean Red Sea port revived under the 2026 Egypt-Eritrea maritime agreement

label: Hamdayet Border Crossing (Sudan)
sub: Main entry point for Tigrayans, including wounded fighters, fleeing into Sudan after the Aug 1-2 Shererina clashes

label: Teleta Gebriel (Aseko, East Arsi)
sub: Site of coordinated May 30-June 1, 2026 attacks that killed at least 37 Orthodox Christians during the election period; OLA denied deliberately targeting civilians

label: Gimbi
sub: Western Oromia town; longstanding site of OLA activity and communal violence in the broader Oromia insurgency

label: Central Oromia (Sheno area)
sub: General area within ~100km of Addis Ababa where the OLA claimed a major March 25, 2026 operation against ENDF forces; figures unverified

label: Semera (Afar)
sub: Afar regional capital near the Eritrean border corridor; Afar authorities accused TPLF-linked elements of cross-border attacks in late 2025

label: Dire Dawa
sub: Federal chartered city; election security incidents contributed to closures among the 143 polling stations shut across Amhara and Oromia on June 1

label: Jimma
sub: Southwestern Oromia city; area of continuing OLA insurgent activity and government counter-operations through 2026

label: Adigrat
sub: Eastern Tigray city; polling was suspended across the entire Tigray region for a second consecutive election cycle

label: Port Sudan (near)
sub: A May 2026 gathering under the disputed 'Tsimdo' banner reportedly drew Sudanese army officers, Eritrean officials, and Ethiopian opposition figures
